SF Symbol → what Android draws. Built 2026-09-20 from the symbols the ported views use at their own shas. `android` names a Material icon or a DesignKit glyph; `unknown` means nobody has checked, and the audit REPORTS those rather than passing them — a silence is not a pass. A wrong pairing is worse than an admitted gap: it turns the gate green over a glyph no one compared.

2026-09-21: extended from 34 to 75 rows. Most of the new ones were verified by LOOKING — the build installed on a Pixel 10 Pro, or an existing Paparazzi golden — rather than by reading both sides, which is the stronger check and the reason `verified` is worth anything. A third class appears here: `— (text only: …)`, where Android draws NO glyph because the iOS symbol sits on a context-menu `Label` and Material menus in this app are text. That is a real pairing, not a gap, and recording it as `unknown` would have hidden a decision behind a silence. Eight rows remain honestly unknown.

rows.note: iOS marks the offline status with an airplane. Android shows "you're offline" as a titled banner with no glyph; the words are the signal.
iOS marks the script card with a terminal glyph; here the monospace `python3 teemoon_verify.py` IS the mark, and an Apple-branded glyph would be wrong on Android anyway.

rows.android: the literal "↓" after the jump title
rows.note: ChainRail: "known code ↓" jumps from an everyday node to its expert section. Trailing the words, as iOS has it.
appearance → font width. Seen on the Pixel.
the CTA's trailing mark. Seen on the Pixel.
a Label on iOS; a plain button here.

rows.android: a tinted circle with Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowForward rotated -90°
rows.note: the composer's send button — the core icon set has no ArrowUpward. Seen on the Pixel.

rows.android: OpenLinkGlyph, or the literal "↗" after a link's text
rows.note: a link out. The drawn glyph leads a row; the arrow trails inline text.
appearance → font size. Seen on the Pixel.
the primer banner above the verification run.
same: a context-menu Label on iOS, a text DropdownMenuItem here.
the chain's OK node and the none screen's positive rows (trustScreen_proof_seededRecord, trustScreen_notAttestable_withTheWayOut).
EnclaveGroupView's verified seal (trustScreen_proof_seededRecord).
the encrypted-model CTA (trustScreen_notAttestable_withTheWayOut). Seen on the Pixel.

iOS gives each 'what you still trust' row a leading glyph — an eye, angle brackets, a cpu. Android renders the three sentences plain. Worth revisiting as a design question, not a mapping one: the glyphs carry no information the sentence lacks, but they do carry rhythm.
the where chip's trailing pair, and the connection section's picker. Seen on the Pixel.
a pending run step, in a 16dp column with the other four status marks so they cannot shift the row.

AddEditProviderScreen's recent-host suggestions. iOS's clock-with-an-arrow says 'you have been here before'; the circular arrow is the nearest mark in this app's own vocabulary, and it already means 'again' on the re-verify row.
places & keys → home machines. Same mark as server.rack on this side; iOS distinguishes the two and Android has one machine glyph.
FableAuditBlock.

rows.android: a filled red circle with "!" in the ground colour (InlineError)
rows.note: the model section's failure mark. Same construction as FilledCircleGlyph — a filled disc with the mark knocked out — at 14dp.
settings → developer mode. Android's Build icon is a WRENCH, not a hammer — the same idea in the Material vocabulary, and the only tool glyph in the core set. Seen on the Pixel.

rows.android: the literal "🔧" in the debug card's header
rows.note: iOS marks the request debug card with a filled hammer. The card is behind developer mode on both sides; here the header line carries the emoji and the provider name.

iOS's `Label("model info", systemImage:)` in a context menu. Android's menus in this app are text-only DropdownMenuItems and its row action is the word "info"; Material context menus do not carry leading icons here.
the chain's INFO node (trustScreen_proof_seededRecord).
the on-device row's mark. Seen on the Pixel.

rows.android: the literal "≡" in the sort capsule
rows.note: model browser → grouping/sort. Seen on the Pixel.
RecipeCardView's "the running recipe".
TrustLadderView+None's on-device hero.
the not-attestable hero, and the degraded chip. Seen on the Pixel.

rows.android: a bordered circle with a centred bar
rows.note: the none screen's negative rows — outlined, not filled, so an absence never borrows a failure's weight.
appearance → color. Seen on the Pixel.
"add cloud key" and the chats list's new-chat button. Seen on the Pixel.
the merge notice. iOS labels it with a stack-minus; Android's Banner is title + body + action with no icon, the same shape as the 'couldn't read your setups' banner beside it.
the machine mark: ProviderIdentityTile's self-hosted fallback, the preset grid's custom tile, the cloud-key picker's custom row. Seen on the Pixel.
the share action. Android's share is the system sheet, reached from a labelled button rather than an icon.

rows.android: a tinted circle with a white rounded square
rows.note: the composer's stop control, present exactly while a generation runs.

rows.android: the literal text "Aa" in the tint colour
rows.note: appearance → font design. iOS's textformat reads as Aa; drawing it as text is the same mark. Seen on the Pixel.

iOS pairs the word with a trash glyph in swipe actions and menus. Android's trailing swipe shows the label, and the long-press menu is text — the destructive colour carries the weight the glyph does there.

rows.android: — (text only: a "couldn't load models" label over its footer)
rows.note: iOS's ContentUnavailableView takes an icon; Android's empty state is a SectionLabel and a GroupFooter, which is how every other empty state in this app reads. An icon on one of them would make it the odd one out.

rows.android: FilledCircleGlyph("×") on a chain node; "✕" on a run step; the word "cancel" on a download row
rows.note: THREE call sites, three answers — the chain mark is a glyph, the step mark is text in a 16dp column, and the download row's is a labelled action rather than a mark at all. Left unverified on purpose: one row cannot honestly pair a symbol that means three things.
the same glyph, failed — drawn from one function so the pair cannot drift apart.
